provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Native mechanism: column 0 is a stripe of markers (6) on a background of 7. Bars lie in rows. A row y is released when four things hold. Its stripe cell is the marker. The next cell inward is background. The first non-background cells of rows y-1 and y+1 have the same colour and sit at the same distance from the stripe. Row y is background at that distance. For each released row, the stripe marker becomes background. A walker then starts one cell inside the stripe and heads inward. It moves straight while the next cell is background. When blocked, it turns into the unique perpendicular background neighbour whose two flanking cells are equal and non-background. With zero or two such openings it stops, and a marker is written at the stop cell. Every walk reads the input grid.

The factory pushes the native inward direction (0,1) through the D4 map: horizontal mirror for d4>=4, then (dr,dc)->(dc,-dr) per clockwise turn. This gives the stripe edge in visible coordinates: left, right, top or bottom. The factory emits a lane accessor cell(lane,t), where t=0 is the stripe edge and t grows inward. It is a direct expression in visible indices, such as (lane, W-1-t) or (H-1-t, lane). Lanes run along the visible axis parallel to the inward direction. The release test is symmetric in lanes y-1 and y+1, so lane order needs no reversal.

The walker runs entirely in visible coordinates. It starts with the visible inward vector (DR,DC) and uses the native turn/opening test. That test treats both perpendiculars and both flanks symmetrically, so it is D4-equivariant without further rewriting. The step bound 4*H*W is invariant. Colour roles are the constants BG=palette[7] and MARK=palette[6]. No other colours are remapped, because bar colours only need to be compared for equality.

The fixtures were hand-checked against this rule, not run. For example, in pair 1 row 5 walks inward, turns up the 4-flanked channel, and stops at the top edge (0,14). Rows 4 and 12 fail the same-x condition. I found no contradiction with a uniform rule.
draft_notes.limitations: Nothing has been executed; the fixture check above was done by hand. Background and marker roles are fixed as palette[7] and palette[6], not inferred from the demos. This matches the constructor, where colours 6 and 7 are reserved for marker and background. The stripe side comes only from d4, so a grid whose stripe sits on a different edge than d4 predicts would not be handled. That cannot occur under the stated episode transform. Grids whose lanes are shorter than 2 cells, or that have fewer than 3 lanes, are returned unchanged; the constructor's domain (width 10..30, odd height 11..29) never produces these. No constructor indexing defects or hidden random tie-breaks affect the visible rule. Walker forks (two openings) deterministically stop, as the design intends.
